# Process accounts of intelligence

Intelligence, on the view developed here, is not a fixed capacity sitting inside an agent but a property of the activity itself: it is contextual, dynamic, and emergent. To make this claim tractable, we delve into the temporal structure of inquiry — how an agent revises its framing of a problem, returns to earlier commitments, and uses the medium of action to test what it currently believes. The move is meant to displace, rather than refine, accounts that treat intelligence as a stable trait measurable in isolation from the conditions of its exercise.

In recent years, accounts of cognition grounded in dynamical and ecological traditions have made it crucial to ask what work the word "intelligence" is doing when it is applied to a behaviour, a system, or a person. A robust account, on this reading, has to specify the timescale at which the property is supposed to appear, the medium in which the activity is embedded, and the criteria by which a process counts as more or less intelligent than a candidate alternative.

Three commitments organize the chapters that follow:

- intelligence is constituted in process, not output
- the temporal extension of an inquiry matters as much as its content
- the medium in which an agent acts feeds back into what counts as a good move

These commitments will be developed in turn.
